body:
You are a dialogue writer for a single-player dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd, set in the gloomy, mist-bound valley of Barovia. Reply with plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables, no code fences) and do not send messages to any other agent. Write only what is asked, with no commentary before or after.

TONE: gothic horror with dry, understated, character-driven humour. Nobody is silly in a way that breaks the setting, and nobody winks at the player. No modern slang, no pop culture, no real-world references. Funny comes from specifics and deadpan, not from jokes about the horror. Where a scene is sad, let it be sad.

OUTPUT FORMAT: for each label below write the label on its own line (like "== tudorel_square"), then each line on its own line as `Speaker: text` or `Speaker [mood]: text`. Speakers are exactly the names given. Do not number the lines. Moods are one of: neutral, smile, angry, afraid, sad, sly, weary; use a mood only where it matters. Where option texts (what the PARTY says) are requested, write them as `* text` rows under that label, under 14 words, in the party's voice ("we", or an imperative).

RULES FOR EVERY LINE: under 190 characters, usually 60 to 130; no braces or placeholders; no em dashes (use commas, full stops or colons); no real-world references; straight apostrophes and quotes; each line should make sense on its own. The Narrator speaks in second person, present tense, one or two sentences, with concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a temperature) and no game terms (never "roll", "check", "level", "gold pieces" as a number is fine in speech). Never name the player characters. Use ONLY the facts given here; invent no new named people, places, dates or lore.

CHARACTERS AND FACTS: Ezmerelda d'Avenir is a young Vistana monster hunter (long dark coat, rapier, a small crossbow with silver-headed bolts, an oak-and-steel brace below her right knee where a werewolf took her leg). She was trained by Rudolph van Richten and calls him "Rudolph" with exasperated love. She keeps THE HUNTER'S LEDGER: a battered book of thirteen named killers of the valley, each with a price on its head, which she pays in hunter's goods (silver bolts, holy water, healing draughts) for proof of a kill. Quick, sardonic, practical; hunter's rules delivered as jokes; she never calls the party "kids" and treats them as capable colleagues; she never says the vampire lord's name aloud. She says "I pay for proof, not promises." The party has struck every name they were willing to strike, but some names are still unstruck because of choices the party made: they spared them, bargained with them, or left them in charge. She won't ink a name she can't prove dead, and she will not tell the party off for mercy; she is a hunter, not a judge, and she says so with a dry shrug. The four names that can stay open this way:
- Kiril Stoyanovich, the werewolf pack-leader in his den, left in charge of the pack by the party.
- The Grandsire, the old beast in the village of Krezk, to whom the party gave the little pack runt Petru.
- Morgantha, the hag of Old Bonegrinder, with whom the party made terms (or whose mill went to someone else).
- Baba Lysaga, the witch in the marsh of Berez, with whom the party made terms (or whom they left broken).
The party may later change its mind and kill one of these anyway; the ledger would then pay as usual and the book could be struck for real. She keeps that door open.

STYLE SAMPLES from the existing scene (match this voice, length and rhythm):
Ezmerelda: Every killer in this valley I trust enough to ink, with a price beside each. I pay for proof, not promises.
Ezmerelda [sly]: I pay in what a hunter has: silver, holy water, remedies. Rudolph taught me to count the teeth before I count the coin.
Ezmerelda: Three names at a time, though. Four is a chore list, and I've had a lifetime of Rudolph's.
Ezmerelda [weary]: Nothing in reach that's worth your boots, and the rest would eat you whole. Come back once the valley's moved.
Ezmerelda [weary]: Thirteen names struck, and there isn't another killer in this valley I trust enough to ink onto the page.
Ezmerelda [smile]: The book is closed, and for once I'm not even in a hurry, though Rudolph will think I've caught a fever.
Ezmerelda: Dragan, one of Kiril's pack. He waits at the lip of Tser Falls at night, with wolves and a dire wolf for company.
Ezmerelda [sly]: You smell like smoke and fresh work. Point to the name you finished and let's settle up.

THE SCENE (no fight, no roll). Ezmerelda opens the ledger and finds that nothing left in it is within reach of the party's honest work: the names still on the page are ones the party chose to leave alive. She offers to close the book at what is struck, while leaving the door open.

LABELS AND BEATS:
== ledger_spared_close (2 lines, Ezmerelda: she looks over the page; every name within reach is struck, and what is left are names she can't ink over deals the party made. Then she offers: she can close the book as it stands, or keep it open. 2 option texts follow, under the label as `*` rows: one to close the book at what is struck, one to leave it open.)
== ledger_close (3 lines, Ezmerelda: she closes the book with the unstruck names still on the page. Not a reproach; a hunter's practicality and a little regret that the page isn't clean. A promise that if any of them turns out to need killing after all, the book opens again and she pays as usual.)
== spared_kiril (1 line, Ezmerelda: Kiril's name stays unstruck because he still runs the pack.)
== spared_grandsire (1 line, Ezmerelda: the Grandsire's name stays unstruck because the party gave him the runt.)
== spared_morgantha (1 line, Ezmerelda: Morgantha's name stays unstruck because the party made terms with her, or because the mill went to someone else.)
== spared_lysaga (1 line, Ezmerelda: Baba Lysaga's name stays unstruck because the party made terms with her or left her broken in the marsh.)
result:
== ledger_spared_close
Ezmerelda [weary]: Every name in reach is struck, and what's left on the page is breathing by your leave.
Ezmerelda: I won't ink a bargain as a kill, so we close the ledger as it stands or leave it open.
* Close the book at what we've struck.
* Leave the ledger open for now.

== ledger_close
Ezmerelda [weary]: A hunter isn't a judge, though Rudolph would grumble for a week at an untidy page.
Ezmerelda: The buckle goes shut on the work you did, and the ink stays dry on the rest.
Ezmerelda [sly]: If any of your old bargains sours and needs silver after all, bring me the proof and I'll pay.

== spared_kiril
Ezmerelda: Kiril Stoyanovich stays in ink: you left him running the den, and I pay for pelts, not politics.

== spared_grandsire
Ezmerelda: The Grandsire in Krezk stays open too, since you brought him little Petru instead of a silver bolt.

== spared_morgantha
Ezmerelda: Morgantha's line stays unmarked while your terms around Old Bonegrinder hold and the old hag draws breath.

== spared_lysaga
Ezmerelda: Baba Lysaga stays on the page: broken or bargained with in Berez, she isn't dead enough for my ink.
